REMARKS
Claims 1–17 and 20 are pending, with claim 1 being independent. Claims 1 and 11 are amended. Claims 18–19 were previously canceled. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the cancelled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.
Applicant-Initiated Interview Summary
A video conference interview regarding the instant matter was conducted on June 24, 2024, between Examiner Cindi M Curry and Applicant’s Shixiong Wang, 79880. Patentability under 35 U.S.C. § 103 was discussed. Applicant thanks the Examiner for her time and consideration in conducting the interview. No agreement was reached. However, the Examiner stated specifying a liquid check valve may move prosecution forward.
Rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103
Childress/Clarke/Struzik/Glaser/Paget
Claims 1, 6, 15, and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over US Patent Publ. No. 20090090724 A1 to Childress et al. (hereinafter “Childress”) in view of US Patent Publ. No. 20220136656 A1 to Clarke et al. (hereinafter “Clarke”), in further view of US Patent Publ. No. 20130197791 to Struzik (hereinafter “Struzik”), in further view of US Patent Publ. No. 20110042520 A1 to Glaser et al. (hereinafter “Glaser”), in further view of US Patent Publ. No. 20230294836 A1 to Paget et al. (hereinafter “Paget”). Office Action, p. 2. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 1 as amended currently recites:
A method for fueling and using an aircraft, wherein the method comprises:
conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, wherein the chamber includes at least one layer of reflective foil within an insulative material, and clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel;
venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank;
storing, using the fuel tank comprising the chamber between the inner wall and the outer wall of the fuel tank, the liquified gas fuel, wherein the chamber is configured to insulate the liquid gas fuel by prevention of condensation of humidity within the fuel tank of the aircraft;
fueling, using a fuel line, the aircraft, wherein fueling further comprises:
filling the fuel tank with the liquified gas fuel to a desired level, wherein the desired level comprises fuel for a plurality of flights plus reserves, wherein a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related insulation of the fuel tank, wherein the sensor is configured to:
detect humidity within the fuel tank; and
convert the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and
removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft; and
preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level; and
flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas fuel.
The Office Action alleges that Childress teaches “clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel” at paragraph [0024] of Childress stating in part “A pressurized gas may be introduced via the inlet into the bladder.” However, the above-quoted language does not disclose “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” The Office has not asserted that Childress teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Accordingly, Applicant submits that Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Childress.
Clarke does not cure the deficiencies of Childress. The Office has not asserted that Clarke teaches, suggests or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant respectfully submits that Clarke does not teach, suggest or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Accordingly, Applicant submits that Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Childress and Clarke, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Struzik does not cure the deficiencies of Childress and Clarke. The Office has not asserted that Struzik teaches, suggests or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant respectfully submits that Struzik does not teach, suggest or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Accordingly, Applicant submits that Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Clarke, and Struzik, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Glaser does not cure the deficiencies of Childress, Clarke, and Struzik. The Office has not asserted that Glaser teaches, suggests or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant respectfully submits that Glaser does not teach, suggest or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Accordingly, Applicant submits that Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Clarke, Struzik, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Paget does not cure the deficiencies of Childress, Clarke, Struzik, and Glaser. The Office has not asserted that Paget teaches, suggests or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant respectfully submits that Paget does not teach, suggest or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Accordingly, Applicant submits that Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Clarke, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Claims 6, 15, and 17 depend, directly or indirectly, on Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over, Childress, Clarke, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant submits that claims 6, 15, and 17 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Clarke, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Childress/Struzik/Glaser/Paget/D’Auvergne
Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Childress, in view of Struzik, in further view of Glaser, in further view of Paget, in further view of US Patent No. 7281682 B2 to D’Auvergne (hereinafter “D’Auvergne”). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 2 depends, directly or indirectly, from Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 2 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
D'Auvergne fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget. The Office has not asserted that D’Auvergne teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that D’Auvergne does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claim 2 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and D’Auvergne, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Childress/Struzik/Glaser/Paget/Wexler/Epstein/Conner
Claims 3 and 5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Childress, in view of Struzik, in further view of Glaser, in further view of Paget, in further view of US Patent No. 6123295 A to Wexler et al. (hereinafter “Wexler”), in further view of US Patent Publ. No. 20150344143 to Epstein et al. (hereinafter “Epstein”), in further view of the NPL titled “What is Aerogel” by Nick Conner (hereinafter “Conner”). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claims 3 and 5 depend, directly or indirectly, from Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Wexler fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget. The Office has not asserted that Wexler teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that Wexler does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Wexler, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Epstein fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Wexler. The Office has not asserted that Epstein teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that Epstein does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, and Epstein, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Conner fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, and Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Conner teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that Conner does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claims 3 and 5 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, Epstein, and Conner, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Childress/Struzik/Glaser/Paget/Wexler/Epstein/Conner/Clark
Claim 4 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Childress, in view of Struzik, in further view of Glaser, in further view of Paget, in further view of Wexler, in further view of Epstein, in further view of Conner, and in further view of US Patent No. 6422514 B1 to Clark et al. (hereinafter “Clark”). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 4 depends, directly or indirectly, from Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, Epstein, and Conner, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 4 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, Epstein, and Conner, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Clark fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, Epstein, and Conner. The Office has not asserted that Clark teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that Clark does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claim 4 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Wexler, Epstein, Conner, and Clark alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Childress/Struzik/Glaser/Paget/Epstein
Claims 7-11, 13, 14, 16, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Childress, in view of Struzik, in further view of Glaser, in further view of Paget, in further view of Epstein. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claims 7-11, 13, 14, 16, and 20 depend, directly or indirectly, from Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Epstein, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 7-11, 13, 14, 16, and 20 are patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Epstein, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Childress/Struzik/Glaser/Paget/Epstein/Benassi
Claim 12 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Childress, in view of Struzik, in further view of Glaser, in further view of Paget, in further view of Epstein, and in further view of US Patent Publ. No. 20120119032 A1 to Benassi et al. (hereinafter “Benassi”). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 12 depends, directly or indirectly, from Claim 1. As noted above, Claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Epstein, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 12 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Epstein, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Benassi fails to cure the deficiencies of Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, and Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Benassi teaches, suggests, or motivates “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” Applicant respectfully submits that Benassi does not teach, suggest, or motivate “venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank.” As such, Applicant submits that Claim 12 is patentably distinguishable over Childress, Struzik, Glaser, Paget, Epstein, and Benassi, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.
Conclusion
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a condition for allowance and respectfully solicit the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
